Korean · Dinner

Japchae

Chewy sweet potato noodles tossed with individually stir-fried vegetables and a sesame-soy dressing. Naturally gluten-free, good hot or at room temperature, and a fixture of every Korean celebration.

★★★★★★★★★★4.7(1,622)Rated 4.7 out of 5 from 1622 reviews 40 min total Serves 6 servings Medium Korean
Jump to Recipe Jump to Method

Why This Recipe Works

Sweet potato starch noodles have no gluten and a very high amylopectin content, giving them their springy chew — but they turn gummy if overcooked, so they are boiled briefly and rinsed. Cooking each vegetable separately keeps colours distinct and prevents the wetter ones from steaming the rest.

Method

Tap a step to highlight it, or turn on Cook Mode for large type and step-by-step focus.

  1. Whisk all the sauce ingredients together and set aside.

  2. Boil the noodles for 6 to 7 minutes until springy and translucent, then drain, rinse briefly under cold water and cut roughly with scissors so they are manageable.

  3. Toss the warm noodles with a third of the sauce immediately so they absorb it and do not stick.

  4. Blanch the spinach for 45 seconds, refresh, squeeze dry and dress with a splash of sesame oil and a pinch of salt.

  5. Stir-fry each remaining vegetable separately over high heat with a little oil and salt: onion 2 minutes, carrot 2 minutes, pepper 90 seconds, mushrooms 3 minutes.

  6. If making the egg garnish, beat the eggs, cook them as a thin flat omelette, then roll and slice into fine ribbons.

  7. Combine the noodles, all the vegetables and the remaining sauce in a large bowl and toss thoroughly with your hands, which distributes it far better than tongs.

  8. Taste and adjust with more soy sauce or sesame oil, then serve warm or at room temperature topped with the egg ribbons and extra sesame seeds.

Chef’s Tips

  • Dress the noodles while warm so they drink up the sauce rather than sitting in it.
  • Toss with your hands. It is the only way to coat glass noodles evenly.
  • Japchae is traditionally served at room temperature, which makes it excellent for taking places.

Pairing Suggestions

  • Soju or a cold lager
  • Serve as part of a spread with bulgogi and kimchi
  • Finish with fresh fruit

Storage & Reheating

Refrigerate 3 days. The noodles firm up when cold; refresh in a hot pan with a splash of water and sesame oil.
